To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mechanical behaviour of concrete exposed to cyclic loading is inhomogeneous, the maximum load level of cyclic loading is more effective than the minimum one, and the P wave ratio is a good precursor of fatigue failure.
the mechanical behaviour of concrete is inhomogeneous under cyclic loading, and the middle part of sample is more prone to failure than top and bottom parts.

the inhomogeneous mechanical behaviour, including the residual strain, energy dissipation and P wave speed, are observed in the top, middle and bottom part of concrete subjected to compressive cyclic loading; and that the inhomogeneity is related to the loading history, the maximum load level and the type of loading (cyclic or monotonic).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhomogeneous behaviour of concrete subjected monotonic and cyclic loadings.
the inhomogeneous behaviour of concrete under monotonic and cyclic loadings, and the findings are expected to be useful for the development of concrete materials and structures

the mechanical behaviour and damage evolution of concrete subjected to different loading strategies, the findings can be used as an important reference to understand the inhomogeneous mechanical behaviour and damage mechanisms of concrete under cyclic loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical behaviour of concrete under cyclic loading is inhomogeneous, the inhomogeneity is mainly related to the loading level and loading strategy.
concrete is a material with inhomogeneous mechanical behaviour, which is affected by loading method and load level.
the inhomogeneous behaviour of concrete is a result of complex interaction of different factors such as material properties, microstructure, loading methods and loading levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
concrete is a heterogeneous material and its mechanical behaviour and fatigue failure are inhomogeneous.
the mechanical properties of concrete are inhomogeneous, and this should be considered in the design of concrete structures.
concrete subjected to monotonically increasing loading is more prone to failure than that exposed to cyclic loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the middle part of the sample has larger residual strains and dissipated energy during cyclic loading.
the mechanical behaviour of concrete is inhomogeneous at the macroscopic level during monotonic and cyclic loadings, and the middle part of the sample is the most sensitive part to the load level.
inhomogeneous behaviour of concrete subjected cyclic loading is a key factor that should be considered in design.
